text:
mike: Heads up — ran into a surprising shutdown behavior in the Go SDK generator streaming in our sample app. Cancelling the ctx doesn't always terminate the stream goroutine, leading to goroutine leaks when requests time out.

jess: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro and SDK version?

mike: repro is tiny, SDK v0.9.2. steps: start generator stream with a 2s timeout, then cancel. goroutine count stays high. sample snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  chunk, err := resp.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
// expecting goroutine to return after ctx cancelled
```

mike: logs show repeated "client: stream read timeout" followed by background retry goroutines.

alex: hmm could be handshake/keepalive retry thread not tied to request ctx. Does the SDK spawn a per-stream reconnect?

tomas: Is this using the generator convenience helper or direct stream API? Some helpers spawn a monitor goroutine for reconnect/backoff.

mike: generator convenience (GeneratorStream). I grepped — there is a background retry loop that uses its own context derived from a parent, but I think we missed wiring cancellation when the user ctx is done.

sandeep: can you try patching the client call to select on ctx and break the recv loop early? e.g.
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
    resp.Close() // signal the stream to stop
    return ctx.Err()
  default:
    chunk, err := resp.Recv()
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
  }
}
```

mike: tried that, it helps for the main goroutine but the retry/handshake goroutine still lingers. I think the higher-level code never cancels the internal backoff context.

jess: can you open a minimal sample repo? I can try to repro locally and add a unit test that fails on goroutine leaks.

mike: created quick sample and ran with `go test -v -run TestGenCancel -race`. leak reproduced. I'm attaching gist: https://gist.example/abcd (contains sampleapp + test).

ci-bot: CI run for mike/sample-gen-cancel (PR #234) completed: 1 failed, 3 passed — leaking-goroutines test failed.

alex: thanks. quick idea: ensure internal backoff uses the request ctx rather than service-level ctx. If that can't be done, we should offer an exported Close() on generator response that cancels internals.

jess: agree. two paths: 1) fix internals to inherit user's ctx, 2) add explicit Close/Shutdown on stream to signal internals. Which is less breaking?

tomas: probably add Close() as short-term, then follow up to wire ctx properly. Keep behavior backwards compatible by making Close optional.

sandeep: I'll draft a small change: expose resp.Close() that cancels internal contexts and stops retry loops. Then update sampleapp. If maintainers agree, we can backport to 0.9.x as a patch.

mike: sweet — thanks. filing issue and PR now. will include the test.

jess: awesome. once PR is up ping @eng-runtime and @devex for review. :thumbsup:

mike: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/789 — includes Close() impl + test.

ci-bot: PR 789 CI: running e2e + unit tests...

alex: quick note for docs: add a short snippet in the Go generator examples showing how to cancel properly (both ctx-based and explicit Close()).

mike: will add a small sample under examples/generator/cancel/ demonstrating both patterns.

jess: closing the thread here — thanks all for quick turnaround. will follow up if more flakes show up.
